stories.title: Pip the Pup
stories.summary: Pip has a red ball. Where did it go?
pages:
Pip is a pup. Pip has a red ball.

Pip likes to run and jump with the ball.

The ball rolls. It rolls past the cat. It rolls past the bed.

Pip sniffs. Where is the ball?

Pip looks in the box. No ball.

Pip looks in the bag. No ball.

The sun is hot. Pip naps in the shade.

The ball was by the tree! Pip is glad. Good pup, Pip.

stories.title: The Big Ship
stories.summary: Sam and Dad watch a big ship come in to the dock.
pages:
Sam and Dad go to the dock. The wind is cold.

Sam has a hat and a red coat.

A big ship is on the sea. It has a long deck.

A fish jumps up. Splash!

The ship comes in. A man ties it up with a rope.

Dad lifts Sam up to see.

"When I am big, I will sail a ship," said Sam.

Dad smiles. "Then I will wave from the dock."

stories.title: Frog and the Rain
stories.summary: Frog waits for rain on a hot day. Then the clouds come.
pages:
It was a hot day by the pond. Frog sat on a stone.

"I need rain," said Frog. "My pond is low."

Duck swam by. "The sky is blue," said Duck. "No rain today."

Frog sighed and sat very still.

Then the wind blew. Grey clouds rolled in.

Drip. Drop. Drip. The rain began to fall.

The pond grew and grew. Frog hopped and sang.

"Thank you, rain!" said Frog. Duck splashed too.

stories.title: The Moon Boat
stories.summary: Mia dreams she sails a boat all the way to the moon.
pages:
Mia could not sleep. She looked out at the bright moon.

A little boat floated by her window.

Mia climbed in. The boat sailed up, up, up, past the trees and the clouds.

The stars were like tiny lamps.

On the moon, it was quiet and soft. Mia jumped very high.

She found a shiny stone and put it in her coat.

The boat took her home. Mia woke up in bed.

Was it a dream? In her coat was a shiny stone.

stories.title: Rabbit's Garden
stories.summary: Rabbit plants a garden, and friends help it grow.
pages:
Rabbit wanted a garden. She dug the soil and planted seeds in tidy rows.

"Grow, little seeds," she said.

Every morning, Rabbit watered the garden. But nothing happened.

She felt sad and sat down on a log.

Her friend Mouse came by. "Seeds take time," said Mouse. "Let's wait together."

They played and talked and watched the sky.

One day, green shoots came up. Then carrots! Then flowers!

Rabbit shared the carrots with all her friends. "A garden is better with friends," she said.

stories.title: The Friendly Dragon
stories.summary: Everyone runs from the dragon, but the dragon just wants a friend.
pages:
High on a hill lived a dragon called Dot. Dot was green and very big.

When people saw Dot, they ran away.

"I only want a friend," said Dot. A tear rolled down her nose.

A girl called Ana heard her and walked up the hill.

"Are you sad?" asked Ana. Dot nodded. "Nobody wants to play with me."

"I will," said Ana. "Can you fly?"

Dot gave Ana a ride over the town. Everyone looked up and waved.

After that, nobody ran from Dot. She had a whole town of friends.

stories.title: The Elephant Who Remembered
stories.summary: Grandma Elephant remembers the way to water when the river dries up.
pages:
The summer was long and dry. The river near the elephants' home became a thin, muddy stream.

The young elephants were thirsty and worried.
Grandma Elephant lifted her trunk and sniffed the air. "I remember a lake," she said slowly. "Beyond the three tall rocks."

The herd walked for a whole day. They passed the first rock, then the second, then the third.

The little ones were tired, but Grandma kept them going.

At last, they saw it: a beautiful lake, full of cool water.

The young elephants splashed and sprayed. "How did you remember?" they asked. Grandma smiled. "Some things are important enough to keep."

stories.title: Adventure on Volcano Island
stories.summary: Two explorers follow an old treasure map to a smoking island.
pages:
Kai and Lena found an old treasure map in their grandfather's attic. In the corner was a drawing of an island with a volcano.

"That's Volcano Island," said Lena. "It's real."

They borrowed a small boat and sailed across the bay. As they got closer, they saw a thin line of smoke rising from the mountain.

"The volcano is still sleeping," said Kai. "Mostly."

The map led them through the jungle, past a waterfall, to a cave covered in green vines. Inside, it was cool and dark.

Lena switched on her torch. Something was shining.

It wasn't gold. It was a box of their grandfather's old notebooks, full of drawings of birds, plants and shells.

"This is the treasure," said Kai quietly. "He wanted us to be explorers too."

stories.title: The Knight Who Could Not Write
stories.summary: A draft story about silent letters. Not reviewed yet.
pages:
Sir Ned was a brave knight, but he found writing hard.

The letters in words like knight and write seemed to hide from him.

A wise owl taught him a trick: some letters are quiet. You write them, but you do not say them.

Sir Ned practised every evening by the fire.
